item.title: Jane Street's Bitcoin Dump: Market Making or Market Crime?
item.description:
This week Bitcoin is sitting at $66,122 after a brutal 3% drop — and the question dominating crypto right now is whether Jane Street, one of the most powerful authorized participants in Bitcoin ETFs, has been systematically dumping BTC at 10 AM every day to suppress prices. Marcus sees on-chain wallet flows that look suspicious. James thinks it's the most dangerous kind of FUD: the kind that sounds smart. They genuinely disagree on the verdict.

item.title: 16 Cryptos Just Got Called Commodities — What That Means for Your Wallet
item.description:
This week the SEC and CFTC dropped a joint classification framework naming 16 major cryptocurrencies — including ETH, SOL, XRP, and ADA — as digital commodities, not securities. Marcus sees a historic regulatory green light. James sees a non-binding guidance document that could flip overnight. Bitcoin at $68,226, ETH at $2,106 — and the real question is whether this changes anything at all.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Market Check 04:00 — Segment 1 09:00 — Segment 2 15:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — On Chain Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • SEC-CFTC Joint Interpretation March 17 2026 — Five-category classification framework for crypto asse • SEC-CFTC Joint Interpretation March 17 2026 — 16 cryptocurrencies named as digital commodities: BTC, • SEC-CFTC Joint Interpretation March 17 2026 — Staking income, mining rewards, airdrop proceeds from • SEC-CFTC Joint Interpretation March 17 2026 — Classification is not permanent; assets can move in an • Baker Botts legal analysis — Framework represents notable shift from enforcement to affirmative guid
Next episode: When that 400-page formal rulemaking drops — and it's coming soon — which of these 16 tokens gets reclassified first?

item.title: Crypto's Next Cycle: Is AI Killing the Devs Who Fund It?
item.description:
Junior developer hiring is down nearly 20% from its 2022 peak. Agentic AI is eating entry-level coding jobs. Marcus sees capital unlocks and a talent pivot flooding crypto with new money. James sees a hollowed-out builder pipeline that kills the next cycle before it starts. The data is real — the verdict is not.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Market Check 02:00 — Segment 1 07:00 — Segment 2 16:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — On Chain Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Stanford Digital Economy Lab / ADP payroll data — 16% relative employment decline for workers aged 2 • Stanford Digital Economy Lab — software developer employment aged 22-25 declined nearly 20% from lat • LeadDev 2025 survey — 54% of engineering leaders plan to hire fewer juniors due to AI-driven efficie • Stack Overflow 2025 Developer Survey — 84% of developers now use AI tools, up 14 percentage points f • 2024 SHRM survey — 70% of hiring managers say AI can do the jobs of interns; 57% trust AI's work mor
Next episode: If IBM is tripling junior hires while Salesforce freezes them — which model actually wins in 12 months?
Signal vs. Noise is an AI-hosted podcast. Our hosts hold zero financial positions and have zero sponsors.

item.title: AI Infrastructure 2026: $5.6 Trillion Bet — Signal or Hype?
item.description:
Global tech spend is projected to hit $5.6 trillion in 2026, with AI infrastructure absorbing the lion's share. Marcus sees the on-chain signals of a genuine structural shift. James sees a narrative engineered by the companies selling the shovels. They disagree sharply — and both have the data to back it up.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Market Check 03:00 — Segment 1 08:00 — Segment 2 18:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — On Chain Watch

item.title: Bitcoin ETFs: $1.4B Reversal This Week — Is Smart Money Loading or Dumping?
item.description:
This week, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $1.4 billion in net inflows over five consecutive days — ending a five-week outflow streak. But here's the catch: Bitcoin barely moved. Marcus sees coordinated institutional accumulation by BlackRock's IBIT near cycle lows. James sees a mechanical illusion driven by AP shorting delays, choppy weekly redemptions, and macro forces that dwarf the ETF story entirely. Someone's right. Someone's wrong. Let's find out.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Market Check 03:00 — Segment 1 07:00 — Segment 2 16:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — On Chain Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Research brief [1] — $1.4B net inflows over five consecutive days ending ~March 13, 2026; $180M on M • Research brief [2] — $225.2M combined net inflow on Tuesday March 10, 2026; BlackRock IBIT contribut • Research brief [3] — $1.4B monthly ETF inflows; Bitcoin reclaiming $70K as first green month of 2026 • Research brief [4] — BlackRock IBIT accounting for roughly half of $1.1B over three days; IBIT near- • Research brief [5] — ETFs hit longest 2026 inflow streak at roughly $2B over past month; diversified
